# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 92 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 92 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_092_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 9

**1** "Now the stones that came from the plain and were fitted into the tower in place of those that were rejected — who are they?" I asked. **2** "These," he said, "are the roots of the white mountain. Since those from the white mountain were all found innocent, the lord of the tower commanded that these from the roots of that mountain be brought, so that the tower might be completed. **3** For he knew that if these stones were placed in the building, they would remain bright, and not one of them would grow dark, as has happened with those brought from the other mountains. **4** But since the tower had to be completed, the lord commanded that these be brought at once and placed in the building." **5** "What is the plain, and what are the other mountains?" I asked. **6** "All these mountains and the plain," he said, "are one world. **7** Therefore the lord summoned all the peoples of the world to bring stones to build the tower, that the tower might be completed. **8** That is why the white stones from the plain are of the same nature as those from the white mountain — for they share the same character. The difference is that those from the plain were taken directly from the world." **9** "But why were so many stones cast out and found not to fit? How many were cast out altogether?" **10** "The first — the round ones," he said, "are the worldly wealthy who, when affliction comes near them and they hear of it, deny their Lord." **11** "And who are the rough ones?" **12** "These are those who have known the truth and have not remained in it; they fell away from the saints, and the rashness and unbelief in their spirit made them rough — therefore they were cast out."

---

*LOGOS: "the roots of the white mountain" indicates that even from the purest community there are gradations; the plain-stones share the nature of mountain-12 innocents.*
